comments.author: kms2026
comments.content:
[Impact]
While CVE-2026-109518 has been patched in the archive for all supported Ubuntu releases, official installation and Live ISO images for actively supported LTS releases (22.04 Jammy, 24.04 Noble, and 26.04 Resolute) still ship with the vulnerable `apt` binary.

This creates a critical chicken-and-egg race condition during fresh deployments:
1. Modern Ubuntu installations immediately initiate background network activity upon boot via `cloud-init`, `unattended-upgrades`, `apt-daily.timer`, or desktop update managers (`update-notifier` / PackageKit).
2. These services reach out to repositories before an administrator reaches a login prompt or has an opportunity to manually apply the security update.
3. In untrusted networks or bare-metal datacenter rollouts without custom pre-patched golden images, machines are exposed to potential MITM package substitution during the initial boot window.

[Workaround]
Mitigating this vulnerability with current official media requires severe operational workarounds in bare-metal environments: physically disconnecting network cables, scripting switch port isolation, or keeping machines air-gapped during installation until a patched `apt` `.deb` package is sideloaded manually prior to bringing network interfaces up.

[Proposal]
Following the approach taken in the recent Debian 13.8 point release (which rebuilt installation and Live media to eliminate this initial deployment vector), please consider prioritizing updated point-release ISOs (e.g., 22.04.6, 24.04.6, 26.04.x) or respinning current LTS media to include the patched `apt` package out of the box.
